messages.content: 你可以幫我找到紐約的四家餐廳，提供義大利菜餚，並符合我素食和無麩質的飲食需求嗎？然後再找四家洛杉磯的餐廳，提供同樣類型的食物，也符合我的飲食需求嗎？

function.name: find_restaurants
function.description: Locate nearby restaurants based on location and food preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

dietary_requirements.description: Special dietary requirements, e.g. vegan, gluten-free.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find 4 restaurants in New York that serve Italian cuisine and meet vegetarian and gluten-free dietary requirements. Then find 4 restaurants in Los Angeles with same criteria.

We have a function find_restaurants that can locate nearby restaurants based on location and food preferences. It accepts location, food_type, number, dietary_requirements. We need to call it twice: once for New York, once for Los Angeles. For each call, we want 4 results. The dietary_requirements should include "vegan" and "gluten-free" or "vegetarian" and "gluten-free". The user says "素食" which means vegetarian, and "無麩質" which means gluten-free. So we should pass dietary_requirements: ["vegetarian", "gluten-free"].

We need to call the function twice. The function returns any. We'll produce the function calls. The user wants the results. So we will call the function for New York first. Then for Los Angeles. Then present the results.

We need to use the function calls. The function signature: find_restaurants({location: string, food_type: string, number: number, dietary_requirements?: string[]}). So we call find_restaurants({"location":"New York","food_type":"Italian","number":4,"dietary_requirements":["vegetarian","gluten-free"]}). Then find_restaurants({"location":"Los Angeles","food_type":"Italian","number":4,"dietary_requirements":["vegetarian","gluten-free"]}).

We need to output the function calls. The assistant should respond with the function calls. The user didn't ask for anything else. So we do that.
